rationale: Set B wins because it treats the causal link between Autocado and flat prices as the land mine, not the headline. A leads with "Chipotle bets a robot can hold the line on menu prices through a year of food-cost inflation," which is exactly the unsupported connection a reporter will stab first. B refuses "Robots are paying for Chipotle's price freeze" and turns the hole into a stronger angle: "Flat prices, rising food costs, undisclosed labor savings: the math behind Chipotle's freeze." That is strategy; A is still trying to make the robot pay the burrito bill without receipts.
gaps_in_A: "Chipotle bets a robot can hold the line on menu prices through a year of food-cost inflation" overstates causality. The update places Autocado and the price pledge side by side; it does not say the robot funds the freeze.
"automation as the implied offset" is the weak hinge. If it is only implied, do not build the lead angle on it until a finance source or unit-economics data makes it real.

"What Chipotle's robots mean for investors and the stock" is refused too broadly. A stock-prediction angle is junk, but a margin-mechanics angle around flat prices, rising food costs, and undisclosed labor savings is legitimate.

"Inside the kitchen where a robot halved the time it takes to make guac" promises scene access the update does not provide. It works only if Chipotle can actually produce a pilot kitchen, crew member, or GM. Otherwise it is a cleaner rollout-operations story.
gaps_in_B: "100 robot-equipped stores out of more than 3,500 cannot offset chain-wide food-cost inflation" is a little too certain without food-cost magnitude, labor savings, or capital cost. Make it a skeptical question, not arithmetic theater.
"being funded by something else" turns a fair inference into a conclusion. The better line is that the company has not explained how the freeze is funded.
"tested at scale" is loose for 100 restaurants in a 3,500-plus-store chain. B later says "still under 3%," which is the sharper, truer frame.
